title: Arbitrary Functors as Modalities in a Linear Calculus
summary: We study modalities in the linear lambda calculus, by interpreting them as endofunctors in monoidal closed categories. We support functors that do not distribute over products, including (co)monads. We also support arbitrary natural transformations as conversion between modalities. We provide a generic categorical semantics, which we then specialise to a sound and complete resource semantics. We use this resource semantics to derive normalisation by evaluation. Along the way, we describe several applications of such models. This work aims at providing a foundation for future programming languages with modalities. The paper is backed by a mechanisation in Agda.

title: A Taxonomy of Predicate Transformer Monads for Specifying Monadic Programs
summary: Monads of weakest precondition predicate transformers are the foundation of several verification frameworks for monadic programs. For specifying monadic computations with nondeterminism and nontermination, in addition to weakest preconditions, we introduce the first strongest postcondition monads covering all combinations of angelic or demonic nondeterminism and partial or total interpretations of nontermination. For extending these base strongest postcondition monads with side effects such as mutable state, monad transformers do not yield the expected monads, so we instead generalize the base monads to arrows and use arrow transformers. We give a taxonomy of weakest precondition and strongest postcondition monads, for the base monads and for their versions with state, and show that the known relationships between under- and over-approximate triples based on predicate transformers already hold at the level of the predicate transformers themselves. We use the predicate transformer monads to define under- and over-approximate triples and, where possible, Dijkstra monads. Finally, we relate these two specification styles.
